title: Slow Cooker-Style Beef Barbacoa
excerpt: There is something wonderfully comforting about a pot of barbacoa simmering in the kitchen, filling the house with the warm scent of chiles, garlic, and cumin. This tender beef is the kind of supper Grandma would set out with warm tortillas, bright lime, and plenty of napkins for a happy family gathering.

Why You'll Love This Barbacoa

  • The beef turns wonderfully tender and shreds easily after a slow, gentle braise.
  • Chipotle, garlic, cumin, oregano, and lime create a deeply savory sauce with a bright finish.
  • Warm corn tortillas and fresh toppings make this a relaxed, build-your-own family dinner.
  • Most of the cooking time is hands-off, giving you plenty of room to set the table and enjoy the evening.
  • Leftovers reheat beautifully for tacos, bowls, and quick lunches.

Ingredients

Gather a few humble ingredients to make this richly flavored barbacoa, with tender beef and plenty of fresh toppings for serving.

  • beef chuck roast - 3 pounds, cut into 3-inch pieces
  • kosher salt - 2 teaspoons
  • black pepper - 1 teaspoon
  • vegetable oil - 2 tablespoons
  • yellow onion - 1 small, quartered
  • garlic cloves - 4
  • chipotle peppers in adobo sauce - 2 canned peppers
  • adobo sauce - 2 tablespoons
  • low-sodium beef broth - 1 cup
  • apple cider vinegar - 2 tablespoons
  • fresh lime juice - 2 tablespoons
  • ground cumin - 2 teaspoons
  • dried oregano - 2 teaspoons
  • ground cloves - 1/2 teaspoon
  • bay leaves - 2
  • corn tortillas - 12 small
  • fresh cilantro - 1/2 cup, chopped
  • white onion - 1/2 cup, finely diced
  • lime wedges - for serving

How to Make Barbacoa

Plan on 20 minutes of prep and 3 hours 15 minutes of cooking time. There is no separate resting time required, though letting the shredded beef sit in its sauce for a few minutes before serving makes every bite especially juicy.

Step 1: Trim the Beef

Trim away any large pieces of excess fat from the beef chuck. Leave a little marbling in place to help the meat stay moist and flavorful as it cooks.

Step 2: Pat the Beef Dry

Use paper towels to pat the beef pieces dry. This small step helps the beef brown instead of steam in the Dutch oven.

Step 3: Season the Beef

Season the beef evenly with the kosher salt and black pepper. Turn the pieces so every side gets a light, even coating.

Step 4: Heat the Oil

Heat the vegetable oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. The oil should be hot before the beef goes in, but it should not be smoking.

Step 5: Brown the Beef

Brown the beef in batches for about 2 minutes per side. Avoid crowding the pot so the pieces can develop a lovely browned crust.

Step 6: Blend the Sauce

Add the onion, garlic, chipotle peppers, adobo sauce, beef broth, vinegar, lime juice, cumin, oregano, and cloves to a blender. Blend until the mixture is smooth and fragrant.

Step 7: Return the Beef

Place all of the browned beef back into the Dutch oven. Arrange the pieces in an even layer so they cook gently in the sauce.

Step 8: Add the Sauce

Pour the blended sauce over the beef, scraping in every last bit from the blender. The sauce should nestle around the meat.

Step 9: Add the Bay Leaves

Add the bay leaves to the Dutch oven. They will lend a subtle, savory flavor during the long braise.

Step 10: Braise the Beef

Cover the Dutch oven and braise the beef at 325°F for 3 to 3 1/2 hours. Keep the pot covered while it cooks so the beef stays surrounded by moisture.

Step 11: Shred the Beef

Shred the beef when it reaches at least 190°F and pulls apart easily with a fork. Remove the bay leaves, then toss the shredded meat with the sauce before serving.

Step 12: Warm and Serve

Warm the tortillas and serve them with the barbacoa, cilantro, diced onion, and lime wedges. Let everyone add their favorite toppings right at the table.

Pro Tips for Making Barbacoa

  • Brown the beef in batches for the best color and deepest flavor.
  • Use low-sodium broth so you can control the salt, especially since adobo sauce can be savory.
  • Keep the Dutch oven covered during braising to prevent the sauce from reducing too quickly.
  • For the easiest shredding, use two forks and pull the beef apart while it is still warm.
  • Taste the sauce before serving and brighten it with an extra squeeze of lime if needed.

How to Serve This Barbacoa

  • Make soft tacos with warm corn tortillas, cilantro, diced onion, and lime.
  • Serve the beef over rice with beans and a spoonful of the flavorful sauce.
  • Add barbacoa to a bowl with shredded lettuce, avocado, salsa, and fresh lime.
  • Set out extra toppings such as sliced radishes, cabbage, or a mild tomato salsa for a cheerful taco spread.

Make Ahead and Storage

Storing Leftovers

  • Cool the barbacoa promptly, then store it with some of its sauce in a covered container.
  • Refrigerate for up to 4 days.
  • Keep tortillas and fresh toppings stored separately so they stay at their best.

Freezing

  • Freeze cooled barbacoa in an airtight container or freezer-safe bag with some sauce to protect the texture.
  • Label and freeze for up to 3 months.
  • Thaw overnight in the refrigerator before reheating.

Reheating

  • Reheat the beef gently in a covered saucepan over low heat with a splash of broth or water.
  • Stir occasionally until the beef is hot throughout.
  • Warm tortillas separately just before serving.

Final Thoughts

This barbacoa brings the cozy comfort of a long-simmered family meal to the table, with tender beef, bright lime, and warm tortillas that make everyone feel at home.

FAQs

Here are a few helpful answers for making and serving this comforting barbacoa.

Can I make barbacoa with a different cut of beef?

Yes. Beef shoulder or another well-marbled braising cut can work, though cooking time may vary. Choose a cut that becomes tender with slow cooking.

How do I know when the beef is ready to shred?

The beef is ready when it reaches at least 190°F and pulls apart easily with a fork. If it still feels firm, cover the pot and continue cooking until tender.

Can I make this barbacoa less spicy?

Yes. Use one chipotle pepper instead of two, or replace some of the chipotle with extra adobo sauce for a gentler smoky flavor.

What can I do with leftover barbacoa?

Use leftovers in tacos, rice bowls, quesadillas, or salads. Keep the meat with a little sauce so it stays moist when reheated.
